elements: Six vertical columns of circles; each full column is one sorted group of 5 elements, smallest at top, largest at bottom
Columns 1-5: five circles each at rows 1..5, all discs identical radius
Column 6 (rightmost, partial group): only three circles, at rows 2, 3, 4 — same disc radius as all others
Row-3 (middle) circle of every column is an open white disk with black outline = that group's median
All other circles filled solid black
Italic serif label 'x' just below-right of the white disk in column 3 (the median of medians)
Straight vertical arrow in each column from the row-4 black circle up to the white disk (row 3)
Straight vertical arrow in each column from the white disk (row 3) up to the row-2 black circle
Curved arrow in each full column arcing from the row-5 bottom circle up to the row-1 top circle, bowing left and clear of the intervening discs
Horizontal leftward arrow from column-4's white disk into x
Long curved leftward arrows from the white disks of columns 5 and 6, arcing high above the intervening white disks and dropping into x's right side
Horizontal leftward arrow from x to column-2's white disk
Long curved leftward arrow from x arcing high over column 2 into column-1's white disk

Rounded-corner stepped gray region covering the two black circles below x in column 3, the white disk plus the two circles below it in columns 4 and 5, and the white disk plus the circle below it in column 6
Small legend swatch pair: white outlined disc = 'group median', black disc = 'other element'
Caption line: 'shaded: elements known to be greater than x'
White page background

interactions.label: Rewind / replay the counting argument
interactions.teaches: How SELECT's guarantee is assembled: the figure opens fully built (medians white, median row ordered, block shaded) and the learner can rewind to see that the shaded area is not assumed but produced — groups of 5, then each group's median, then x as the median of those medians, then the block of elements the arrow chains force above x.
interactions.notes: Default and reset state is the final, fully-assembled figure identical to the source; earlier states strip layers away rather than build them up.

interactions.teaches: Clicking x (or any shaded circle) brightens the two-step chain that certifies its ordering — element > its own group median > x — showing that an element is known to exceed x without ever being compared to x directly.
interactions.notes: Non-participating circles and arrows dim; the certifying chain is drawn in an accent color.

interactions.label: Shade elements known to be
interactions.teaches: The partition guarantee is symmetric: flipping the shading to the mirror block in the upper-left shows that at least ~3n/10 elements are forced below x just as at least ~3n/10 are forced above it. Caption text updates with the toggle.
Hovering a circle names its role (group member, group median, or x) and states which orderings are already known for it, keeping labels off the crowded diagram until asked for.

demo_steps.title: The finished picture
demo_steps.narration: This is the whole argument at once: six sorted groups, each group's median in white, arrows ordering the medians around x, and the gray block of elements that must be greater than x. The next steps rewind it to show where the block comes from.

demo_steps.title: Rewind: groups of five
demo_steps.narration: Strip everything back. The n elements are laid out as columns of 5, each column sorted top (smallest) to bottom (largest) by its internal arrows. The rightmost column is a leftover partial group of 3.

demo_steps.title: Mark the group medians
demo_steps.narration: The middle circle of each group turns white: that group's median, already known to be greater than two elements and less than two elements in its own column.

demo_steps.title: Choose x, the median of medians
demo_steps.narration: Horizontal and arcing arrows along the row of white disks order the medians themselves. x is their median: half the medians are at least x, half are at most x.

demo_steps.title: Count what must be greater
demo_steps.narration: Each median greater than x drags its two larger group-mates with it. The shaded stepped block collects every element the arrow chains force above x — at least about 3n/10 of the input — so the partition can never be badly lopsided.

demo_steps.title: The mirror-image half
demo_steps.narration: Flipping the shading to the other side shows the symmetric block forced below x, giving the matching 3n/10 bound and hence the linear-time recurrence.

plan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D diagram in the XY plane (z=0), front-on orthographic. Column centers at X = -6.5, -3.9, -1.3, +1.3, +3.9, +6.5 (spacing 2.6). Row centers at Y = +4.4 (row1), +2.2 (row2), 0.0 (row3 = white-disk/median row), -2.2 (row4), -4.4 (row5). EVERY disc, including those in partial column 6, has identical radius 0.45. Columns 1-5 have circles at all five rows; column 6 has circles ONLY at rows 2, 3, 4. Row-3 circle of all six columns is white fill (#FFFFFF) with a 0.09-thick black outline; every other circle is solid black (#000000). Italic serif 'x', cap height ~0.8, at (-0.65, -0.80), just below-right of column-3's white disk — visible in every phase from 'median-of-medians x' onward AND in the default shaded phase. Arrows: black, shaft 0.085 thick, head 0.45 long x 0.32 wide, tail at the larger element, head at the smaller. Per full column: straight row4->row3, straight row3->row2, and ONE long curved arrow row5->row1 drawn as a cubic Bezier whose control points sit 1.6-1.8 units to the LEFT of the column axis (control points near (cx-1.7, -2.4) and (cx-1.7, +2.4)) so the arc clears the row-2/3/4 discs entirely with visible white gap; column 6 has only row4->row3 and row3->row2. Median-row arrows all point LEFT into or out of x: col4 white -> x straight horizontal along Y=0; col5 white -> x as an arc peaking ~1.6 above Y=0; col6 white -> x as an arc peaking ~2.6 above Y=0 (arcs must clear the white disks they pass over by at least 0.5); three arrowheads converge on x's upper-right. x -> col2 white straight horizontal; x -> col1 white as an arc peaking ~1.6 above Y=0 over column 2. Gray shaded region: fill #B5B5B5, drawn BEHIND circles and arrows at z=-0.01, rounded convex corners radius ~0.6, stepped outline enclosing column-3 rows 4-5, columns 4-5 rows 3-5, and column 6 rows 3-4; spans roughly X = -2.3 to +7.6, top edge Y = +0.95 across columns 4-6, stepping down to Y = -1.25 over column 3, bottom edge Y = -5.3 under columns 3-5 stepping up to Y = -3.1 under column 6 (no row-5 disc there). The 'less than x' mirror region is the 180-degree rotation of this shape about x's center: column-3 rows 1-2 plus columns 1-2 rows 1-3. Legend at bottom-left, outside the diagram bounds (around X=-7.5, Y=-6.6): a white outlined disc radius 0.35 labeled 'group median' and a black disc radius 0.35 labeled 'other element'. Caption centered under the figure at Y=-7.4: 'shaded: elements known to be greater than x' (text swaps with sideToggle). Background white.
plan.notes: Orthographic camera looking down -Z; all geometry flat. Circles as CircleGeometry with a separate ring mesh for the white disks' outline. Arrow shafts as Line2 / TubeGeometry with constant screen-space width; heads as flat triangles. All curved arrows are CubicBezierCurve3 sampled to ~48 points so the left-bowing column arcs and the high median-row arcs read cleanly; verify by collision test that no arc passes within 0.15 of any disc edge. Gray region built as a THREE.Shape with explicit stepped outline and arc()-rounded convex corners, then ShapeGeometry. Phase changes fade layers with 250 ms opacity tweens; the app's initial load and any Reset restore the LAST phase ('shade known-greater') plus sideToggle='greater than x' so the default view matches the source figure exactly. Click-highlight dims non-participating elements to 25% opacity and redraws the certifying chain in #D2402A at 1.4x width; raycast against slightly enlarged invisible hit discs. Hover tooltips as a DOM overlay positioned by projecting circle centers. Legend and caption rendered as DOM text pinned to projected world anchors so they stay crisp.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a schematic array of circles arranged in six vertical columns, with arrows drawn among them and part of the field sitting on a gray background. Five columns hold five circles each, evenly stacked from top to bottom, while the rightmost column holds only three. In every full column the circle in the middle position is an open white disk and the remaining circles are filled solid black. The white disk in the third column from the left carries the italic label x. Straight vertical arrows within each full column run upward from lower circles to the middle disk and from that disk to the circle above, and long curved arrows arc from a column's bottom circle to its topmost one. Along the row of white disks, horizontal arrows point inward toward x: the disks in the fourth through sixth columns send arrows leftward into x, with farther ones curving above intervening columns, and x in turn sends arrows leftward to the disks in the second and first columns. A rounded gray region with stepped edges covers the two circles below x in its own column together with the white disk and every circle beneath it in each column to the right. Because each arrow encodes an ordering between two elements, the shaded block gathers the elements the arrow chains place on one side of x, turning a counting argument about the quality of a partition into a visible area.
authoredInteractions:
- Button for stepping through SELECT's proof phases: group into fives, mark group medians, choose x, then shade elements known greater than x; each press adds only the next visual layer, making the counting argument build deliberately.
- Click x to highlight all arrow chains that certify comparisons to the median-of-medians; the affected circles and arrows brighten, showing why elements on one side of x can be counted without direct comparison to every item.
- Toggle between known-greater and known-less regions; the shaded block switches sides of x, making the symmetric partition guarantee visible for both halves of the proof.
authoredContext: We now examine a selection algorithm whose running time is O.n/ in the worst case. Like RANDOMIZED-SELECT, the algorithm SELECT finds the desired element by recursively partitioning the input array. Here, however, we guarantee a good split upon partitioning the array. SELECT uses the deterministic partitioning algorithm PARTITION from quicksort (see Section 7.1), but modified to take the element to partition around as an input parameter. The SELECT algorithm determines the ith smallest of an input array of n > 1 distinct elements by executing the following steps. (If n D 1, then SELECT merely returns its only input value as the ith smallest.) 1. Divide the n elements of the input array into bn=5c groups of 5 elements each and at most one group made up of the remaining n mod 5 elements. 2. Find the median of each of the dn=5e groups by first insertion-sorting the elements of each group (of which there are at most 5) and then picking the median from the sorted list of group elements. 3. Use SELECT recursively to find the median x of the dn=5e medians found in step 2. (If there are an even number of medians, then by our convention, x is the lower median.) 4. Partition the input array around the median-of-medians x using the modified version of PARTITION. Let k be one more than the number of elements on the low side of the partition, so that x is the kth smallest element and there are nk elements on the high side of the partition. 5. If i D k, then return x. Otherwise, use SELECT recursively to find the ith smallest element on the low side if i < k, or the .i k/th smallest element on the high side if i > k. To analyze the running time of SELECT, we first determine a lower bound on the number of elements that are greater than the partitioning element x. Figure 9.1 helps us to visualize this bookkeeping.

interactions.teaches: How SELECT's guarantee is assembled: first partition the input into groups of 5 and sort each column, then pick each group's median, then take the median of those medians as x, and only then can the block of elements forced to lie on one side of x be counted.

Clicking x brightens every arrow chain that certifies an ordering with x, showing that an element is known to be greater than x through a two-step chain (element > its group median > x) without ever being compared to x directly.

interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera looking down -Z; all geometry is flat. Circles as CircleGeometry (or instanced meshes) plus TubeGeometry/Line2 for arrow shafts and ConeGeometry-style flat triangles for heads. Curved arrows: QuadraticBezierCurve3 sampled into a Line2 with constant screen-space width so arcs read cleanly at any zoom. Gray region: build as a Shape with the stepped outline and rounded corners (Shape.roundedRect-style arcs at each convex corner) extruded to a ShapeGeometry, z = -0.01. Phase stepping should fade elements in with short (250 ms) opacity tweens rather than hard pops; earlier layers stay visible. Click-highlight: dim non-participating circles/arrows to ~25% opacity and draw the certifying chains in a saturated accent (e.g. #D2402A) with slightly thicker lines; raycast against invisible slightly-enlarged circle hit discs. Toggle animates the gray shape morphing/cross-fading between the two stepped outlines. Hover tooltips as DOM overlay positioned by projecting the circle center.

discrepancies: Default state (step 1 / phase 0) does not look like the source: the six group medians are still black rather than white-with-black-ring, the horizontal median-row arrows are absent, the 'x' label is hidden, and the gray shaded block is not drawn — the defining features of the CLRS figure only appear after clicking through to steps 3–4.

The source shows a single gray stepped region (elements known greater than x); the generated figure adds a mirror-image 'less than x' region that is not in the original (mitigated by being behind a toggle).

Arrow arc geometry differs slightly: in the source the long bottom-to-top curves sweep well left of the column and the median-row curves arc high over the columns; the generated curves are shallower and the long column curves cross close to the circles, making the column arrow bundles read slightly more cluttered.
Circles in the rightmost (partial) column appear slightly smaller/thinner than the rest in the render, whereas the source uses identical disc sizes across all columns.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and well-built reconstruction of the CLRS median-of-medians figure with correct column/arrow topology, correct stepped shading, and a rich, pedagogically meaningful set of interactions (phase buttons, side toggle, chain highlighting, hover roles, guided walk-through); the main weakness is that the default state is the stripped-down 'groups of 5' stage, so at first glance it lacks the white medians, median-row arrows, x label and gray region that make the source recognizable.
action_items: Set the initial state to the fully-assembled figure (white medians + median-row arrows + x label + gray 'greater than x' block), and let the phase buttons/walk-through rewind to the build-up stages instead of starting there.
Show the italic 'x' label whenever the median-of-medians disk is white (phase >= 1) and consider a small caption such as 'shaded: elements known to be > x' to mirror the source caption.

Tune the Bezier control points so the long column curves bow further left (clear of the circles) and the median-row curves arc higher, matching the source's arrow routing; ensure all disc radii, including the partial column, are identical.
Add a brief visual legend distinguishing white (group median) vs black (ordinary element) discs so the phase-0 all-black state is not mistaken for the finished figure.
plan_action_items: Plan the default/reset state to be the complete source figure rather than step 1 of the build-up sequence.

The 'less than x' mirror region is the 180-degree rotation of this shape about x's center: column-3 rows 1-2 plus columns 1-2 rows 1-3. Legend at bottom-left, outside the diagram bounds (around X=-7.5, Y=-6.6): a white outlined disc radius 0.35 labeled 'group median' and a black disc radius 0.35 labeled 'other element'. Caption centered under the figure at Y=-7.4: 'shaded: elements known to be greater than x' (text swaps with sideToggle). Background white.
plan.notes: Orthographic camera looking down -Z; all geometry flat. Circles as CircleGeometry with a separate ring mesh for the white disks' outline. Arrow shafts as Line2 / TubeGeometry with constant screen-space width; heads as flat triangles. All curved arrows are CubicBezierCurve3 sampled to ~48 points so the left-bowing column arcs and the high median-row arcs read cleanly; verify by collision test that no arc passes within 0.15 of any disc edge. Gray region built as a THREE.Shape with explicit stepped outline and arc()-rounded convex corners, then ShapeGeometry. Phase changes fade layers with 250 ms opacity tweens; the app's initial load and any Reset restore the LAST phase ('shade known-greater') plus sideToggle='greater than x' so the default view matches the source figure exactly. Click-highlight dims non-participating elements to 25% opacity and redraws the certifying chain in #D2402A at 1.4x width; raycast against slightly enlarged invisible hit discs. Hover tooltips as a DOM overlay positioned by projecting circle centers. Legend and caption rendered as DOM text pinned to projected world anchors so they stay crisp.
